newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Queensland Metals sees modest loss.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Queensland Metals sees modest loss.

text.p: Magnesium producer Queensland Metals Corp said on Tuesday it expects a modest loss for the current year but that subsequent years were forecast to record profitable operations.
Queensland Metals managing director Creagh O'Connor said the company's financial position was sound with more than A$37.5 million in liquid funds.
"Whilst a modest loss is forecast for the 1996/97 financial year, subsequent years are forecast to record profitable operations," he said.
O'Connor told the annual meeting that a successful expansion of the company's Queensland Magnesia Project (QMAG) was critical to QMC's future.
"Success in this area can provide us with the potential to embark on other projects," he said.
Discussions with QMAG's syndicate banks on project debt refinancing were continuing, O'Connor said.

QMC chairman Michael Hamson said engineering and construction work on the QMAG project in North Queensland was underway at a cost of A$28 million which would see expansion of deadburned magnesia facilities rising by 50 percent to 120,000 tonnes a year and electrofused magnesia by 33 percent to 40,000 tonnes a year.
O'Connor said the company hoped to lift tonnage in the current year, despite a downturn in production in the September quarter.

"It is anticipated that the market outlook will be clearer at the end of the December quarter as negotiation will have been held with most customers for their requirements for calendar year 1997," O'Connor said.
He said the company's Magmetal project was also progressing towards building and operating a large scale demonstration plant.
"Based on the current outlook, demand for magnesium is extremely bright and expected to exceed 500,000 tonnes annually by the early part of the next decade," he said.
QMC reported a net loss of A$8.33 million for the year ended June 30 1996 compared with a A$18.76 million loss in the previous year.
Normandy Mining Limited through its wholly-owned subsidary Commerical Minerals Ltd is now QMC's largest shareholder with about 31 percent of the company's capital.
QMC shares were one cent lower at A$1.24 at 12.45 p.m. (0245 GMT).
